due_when.clears_when: manager/SKILL.md (and/or git-actions/SKILL.md) documents the merge-slot-claim precondition as a step before calling merge_pull_request / enable_pr_auto_merge.

routed_to: DOCS-DRIFT | BACKLOG-BURNDOWN-2 2026-10-04 re-read at HEAD: still applies — grep claim_merge_slot|merge-slot in manager and git-actions SKILL.md: no matches (grep found positives elsewhere in repo scripts).
what: [operating-model] The merge-slot-claim mechanism is real and load-bearing: .claude/settings.json installs a PreToolUse hook blocking mcp__github__merge_pull_request / enable_pr_auto_merge unless scripts/ops/claim_merge_slot.py --branch-claim --branch <branch> --held-by <session-id> has run and its file is committed (.github/merge-slots/<slug>.json + .github/pr-landing/<slug>.json), and scripts/ci/check_pr_landing.py (R13) fails a PR that arms auto-merge without the claim. .claude/skills/manager/SKILL.md -- the skill that explicitly owns merging -- never mentions claim_merge_slot.py, .github/merge-slots/, or this guard; neither does .claude/skills/git-actions/SKILL.md. A manager session run on Claude Code on the web (where the PreToolUse hook is measured to not fire, per the guard's own comment citing '1,379 consecutive Hooks: Found 0 total hooks in registry' log lines) has no way to learn this precondition from either skill and could form a false belief that direct merging is unconditionally safe.
